decision_reason: OpenStad headless is a mature, widely used open-source municipal participation platform with official government evidence and deployment guidance, but the whole monorepo's license scope is inconsistent in current first-party records. The root LICENSE.md and package manifests say MIT, publiccode.yml says ISC, and some bundled widget CSS carries EUPL-1.2 notices. Hold until the maintainers clarify whether those files are retained third-party/legacy works or included in the current platform-wide grant.

government_provenance.note: The manifest names Gemeente Amsterdam as organization and lists multiple participating municipalities/provinces as funders and users; the official IPLO government page says Amsterdam and other municipalities developed/offered the open-source platform.

public_source.note: The canonical public headless monorepo exposes API, CMS, authentication/image services, widgets, deployment charts, and installation documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root license text is MIT, but current publiccode.yml says ISC and bundled widget CSS contains EUPL-1.2 file-level notices; the effective grant for the complete application family is not unambiguous from reviewed materials.

primary_evidence.note: The Dutch government's IPLO page describes OpenStad as an open-source municipal participation platform developed by Amsterdam with other municipalities; official OpenStad documentation and website provide setup, deployment, and administrator guidance and report use by many public organizations.

product_identity: OpenStad headless: municipal digital-participation platform monorepo
agency: Municipality of Amsterdam (originating public sponsor), with participating Dutch municipalities and provinces
license: Unresolved for the complete monorepo: root LICENSE.md states MIT (Gemeente Amsterdam); publiccode.yml says ISC; some widget CSS retains EUPL-1.2 notices; dependencies and bundled assets may carry separate licenses
family_note: The assigned Amsterdam repository URL is now represented by the `openstad/openstad-headless` canonical repo per its current publiccode URL. Treat this as one current headless platform monorepo; do not split its apps/packages into separate products or merge the older legacy OpenStad codebase without separate review.
status_note: First root LICENSE.md was MIT in commit https://github.com/openstad/openstad-headless/commit/cd458bb80b34774149ac074d0e46d2017553d208 (2020-03-27); a new root MIT grant was added in 2025 and LICENSE renamed/updated at https://github.com/openstad/openstad-headless/commit/575730185860b3d2f9cd8169c90270ed823c1e12. Current publiccode.yml still says ISC and source CSS includes EUPL-1.2 notices, so record 2020 as first licensed-source year but hold the present whole-product license claim for clarification.

decision_reason: Belastingdienst's Paas Operator is a stable Kubernetes/OpenShift operator with versioned releases, deployable installation manifests, and substantial administrator/user guidance. It creates a controlled multi-tenant project environment with CI/CD, observability, and identity capabilities. The product identity is the operator, not the separately named `opr-paas-cli` companion tool.

government_provenance.note: The manifest names the Tax Administration of the Netherlands (Belastingdienst) as repository owner and copyright owner; the README carries the same agency copyright and the source is maintained under the official Belastingdienst organization.

public_source.note: The public Go repository contains operator/controller source, CRDs, release/install manifests, tests, and administrator/developer documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the actual current LICENSE.md: EUPL v1.2. The README states copyright 2024, Tax Administration of The Netherlands; dependencies retain their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The agency-maintained administrator guide documents production installation and the releases page supplies generated installation manifests; the stable publiccode status and detailed end-user/admin guides meet the agency-distributed release pathway.

product_identity: Paas Operator: Kubernetes/OpenShift multi-tenant Project-as-a-Service operator
agency: Tax Administration of the Netherlands (Belastingdienst), Ministry of Finance
license: EUPL-1.2 for the operator source; dependencies retain their own licenses
family_note: Review only the Kubernetes/OpenShift operator here. The project links a separate `opr-paas-cli`; do not automatically include or claim that companion repository's license or identity.
status_note: The first LICENSE.txt was Apache-2.0 in https://github.com/Belastingdienst/opr-paas/commit/f950f28951a08ec856daeb25426c5761b53559f1 dated 2023-11-29; it changed to EUPL-1.2 in https://github.com/Belastingdienst/opr-paas/commit/618d414d51dcc452cde020a40b5612700ab2e6f0 (same date). First defensible licensed-source year is 2023, not the publiccode 2026 releaseDate.

decision_reason: This is a small beta conversion utility for transforming DCAT-AP-NL 3.0 metadata into API-register input, but the license declaration conflicts: the root LICENSE and publiccode.yml say EUPL-1.2 while package.json says ISC. The package is not a clearly versioned/distributed software release (generic package name `dcat`, no test suite, no install/use instructions beyond the requirements mapping), and I found no primary evidence of external adoption; hold pending license-scope and product-distribution clarification.

government_provenance.note: The manifest names Stichting Geonovum as main copyright owner and describes conversion for the Dutch API Register; the API Register's official documentation identifies developer.overheid.nl and Geonovum as its maintainer contact.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes a Node.js conversion script and example RDF/XML/DCAT files without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE and publiccode.yml state EUPL-1.2, but package.json declares ISC; the repository does not document whether the npm package metadata is stale or whether a different portion is licensed under ISC.

primary_evidence.note: The README documents input validation rules/process but not an installation or release workflow; package.json has a placeholder test command that exits with an error, and no published package/release or external deployment was found.

product_identity: DCAT-AP-NL 3.0 to Dutch API Register metadata-conversion utility
agency: Stichting Geonovum (developer.overheid.nl/API Register team; public-sector standards organization)
license: Unresolved: root LICENSE and publiccode.yml say EUPL-1.2; package.json says ISC
family_note: This is a converter utility associated with the separate API Register application; do not merge it with either the API Register frontend or backend product, and do not infer full API Register functionality from this script.
status_note: The EUPL-1.2 LICENSE file and publiccode.yml were added on 2026-04-01 in https://github.com/developer-overheid-nl/dcat2don/commit/40a5ea2f1de125b486219605ef946ff97a051b7a, but package.json still says `license: ISC` and `name: dcat`; first licensed-source year cannot be safely stated until maintainers clarify the discrepancy and intended distribution.
